correctness.rationale: An orbit simplex contains one vertex for each distinct prime factor of its permutation order; therefore its conjugation stabilizer fixes every vertex and the integral quotient cellular chain groups have one generator for each nonidentity cycle type. Deleting the primary component at prime \(p\) splits an original \(L\)-cycle into \(p^{v_p(L)}\) cycles of length \(L/p^{v_p(L)}\), giving the exact oriented cellular differential. Exhaustive partition enumeration checks all cycle types for ranks 1..15. Free-edge peeling eliminates all two-cycles through rank 14 (rounds 1;2;5;8,1;12,3) and leaves precisely four tetrahedral faces at rank 15 (rounds 15,4,1). Six pair edges show their integer kernel is generated by the primitive alternating tetrahedral shell. Independent modular ranks of the second boundary map for ranks 10..15 are 1,2,5,9,15,23, respectively, over both the fields with 101 and 103 elements. Every permutation involving four distinct primes moves at least 2+3+5+7=17 letters, so there are no three-cells through rank 15 and second homology equals the kernel of the second boundary map. The independent standalone verifier reproduces these finite exact certificates.

value.rationale: The geometric conjugacy schematic is a natural central construction in the newly developed finite-group clique complex, but its first genuine two-dimensional orbit homology is not determined by the known full-complex connectivity or sheaf calculations. The 15-letter boundary is the first tetrahedral shell from four different prime cycle lengths, and the complete free-edge elimination proves both sharpness and uniqueness, rather than a routine isolated numeric Betti number. It supplies an explicit primitive cycle with a natural group-theoretic interpretation and a reproducible method for subsequent small-rank quotient topology investigations. No unsupported infinite-family inference is made.
